title: Introduce soft-fuse sanctuary for transient region overload mitigation
author: Priya Anand
description: Context: We saw two transient zone outages in the last quarter where sudden traffic surges caused regional controllers to flip circuits too aggressively, resulting in a cascade of tenant evictions and noisy failovers. This PR introduces a lightweight "soft-fuse" layer that sits between regional health signals and the circuit breaker to provide a short, silent absorb window for spikes that match a transient signature. Motivation: Reduce noisy mass-evictions and prevent unnecessary global failover during short-lived pressure bursts. Goals: 1) absorb sub-second to multi-second surges without creating long-lived penalty states; 2) emit telemetry to distinguish soft-fuse events from hard circuit trips; 3) provide safe rollout with immediate rollback and canary settings. Design summary: - Soft-fuse controller: evaluates rate and latency jitter signatures for a specified region, and can transiently apply a soft-fuse state which throttles non-critical backends and increases internal admission thresholds without marking the region as unhealthy. - Decay model: soft-fuse has a configurable exponential decay and a max duty window to avoid masking sustained overloads. - Telemetry: new metrics soft_fuse_engaged{region,reason}, soft_fuse_duration_seconds and a histogram for pre/post latency to validate effect. - Policy hooks: soft-fuse integrates with existing SLO enforcer to adjust per-tenant weight only while active; on fuse expiration the policy reconciler runs a quick validation pass to avoid abrupt eviction waves. Rollout and operational plan: 1) feature flag gated off by default; 2) enable in canary region (us-west-2) for 48h with metric alarm for continued degradation; 3) if telemetry shows reduced eviction rate and no higher end-user latency percentile, expand to 50% regions; 4) provide immediate kill switch via Console and CLI. Backwards compatibility: No API changes. Controller lives behind runtime feature flag and is opt-in per-region via config. Tests and validation: - Unit tests for decay math and policy transitions added. - Integration harness simulates jittery traffic; included test scenarios for transient spike and sustained overload. - Load lab run on canary showed 27% fewer tenant evictions during 10x short bursts. Risks and mitigation: - Risk of masking sustained overload: mitigated by max duty cycle and a hard circuit that still trips if SLOs are violated for configured window. - Telemetry blind spots: added high-cardinality tags for region and tenant class, and a conservative default sampling for raw traces. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-2123) - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Telemetry dashboards and alerts (ops/dashboard/soft-fuse) - [x] Feature flag gating and Console controls - [x] Rollout plan in release notes Release notes: "Add soft-fuse sanctuary: transient surge absorber that reduces noisy mass-evictions; opt-in per-region via runtime config. See ENG-2123 for details."

review_comments: Ethan Cole: Overall this looks good. Two requests: 1) make the default duty window smaller (10s) and 2) add a guard in the reconcilers so we don't re-apply tenant weight changes if the tenant had been manually adjusted. The canary plan looks safe.
Priya Anand: RE Ethan: lowered default duty window to 8s (commit a1f3c8b) and added a reconcilers guard to skip manual overrides (commit c7e9f45).
Marta Ruiz: Can we ensure the metrics include an explicit tag for "candidate_reason" so SRE can filter by spike type? Also add a short circuit for controlplane signals that are older than 5s.
Priya Anand: Added candidate_reason tag and controlplane age guard. Updated telemetry docs in ops/soft-fuse-sanctuary.md.
Linus Park: Integration test flaked once on CI (timing). Please mark the harness test as stable and add a retry loop; also confirm CPU impact is <1% in controller in production runs.
Priya Anand: Added retry loop and micro-benchmark; controller CPU median is 0.4% in canary runs. Rerun CI.
